entities.summary: Bernardo de Iriarte was a Spanish politician and diplomat born in 1773 in Valencia, Spain. He served as the Minister of Justice and Foreign Affairs under King Ferdinand VII, playing a key role in shaping Spain's relations with Europe during the early 19th century. His diplomatic efforts helped to establish Spain as a major player in the Congress of Vienna, where the post-Napoleonic order was established. Iriarte's tenure was marked by tensions with the liberal factions within Spain, ultimately leading to his resignation in 1820. He died on July 13, 1814, at the age of 41. Iriarte's legacy is complex, reflecting both the conservative and liberal currents of Spanish politics during this period.
